correctness.rationale: For a four-person group the possible state-changing focal-agent update occurs exactly at one-versus-three splits, which are exactly odd group parity. The active-edge vector is therefore the mod-two incidence product. Rank-nullity gives all attainable fibers and frozen counts; the orthogonal-complement identity gives precise activity constraints. Nonzero incidence rows make each marginal a fair bit and joint independence equivalent to full row rank. All-even incidence rows put the all-ones state in the kernel, proving the consensus-only criterion. The dense construction and dependent triple are explicitly evaluated. The uniqueness among group sizes s>=3 follows by permutation-invariant affine Boolean functions. Standalone full-state enumeration passed 226656 configurations on 3537 hypergraphs.

value.rationale: The exact dynamical-to-coding reduction is motivated by the difference between fixed-group opinion paralysis and the annealed consensus calculations in the source paper. It determines all frozen configurations and their number for arbitrary topology, characterizes every attainable group-activity pattern and its probability under unbiased initialization, and gives sharp structural criteria for independence and consensus-only freezing. In the six-person triple-overlap example a parity dependency forbids simultaneous activity, whereas a complete dense family admits only the two consensus frozen configurations. This is a complete natural structural classification, not a parameter tweak, numerically chosen slice or known-table recomputation.
